description: Exact RGBs in M3's final 16-color quantized palette eligible for palette-variant remapping. 'top' = the vest (M3's dominant, most visually prominent upper-body garment) — the cream shirt underneath is intentionally NOT a remap family; see note. Skin and hair (including eyebrows) are never remapped, matching the roster-integration structural decision (#2).

top.note: Dominant vest fill (verified via strap/collar-clear sample rectangles on front chest + back).

Second fold-shading tone, near-equal pixel count to vest-main; the vest's painterly multi-tone shading (matches the source reference) uses several close browns, but only these two came back clean against both the pure-hair sample and the pure-trousers sample.

trousers.note: Dominant, and only safely-usable, trousers tone. M3's palette has just 2 candidate trouser tones total; the other ((97,68,29)) is excluded (see note) leaving trousers as a single-tone family, same shape as F1's flat blouse-main.

excludedFromRemap.note: M3 needed the deepest cross-check of the roster so far (full-file pixel scans, not just sample rectangles, because the vest/trousers 'dark brown' cluster is unusually tight against hair/eyebrow tones at only 16 total colors). (77,41,18) is excluded from 'top' despite reading as a vest-adjacent brown in the ASCII legend — a full-image scan found it is M3's actual EYEBROW color (confirmed by a zoomed crop), so remapping it would recolor the eyebrows. (97,68,29) is excluded from both families — it is a triple-shared generic shade tone appearing in hair-shadow, vest fold-shading, AND trousers-shade. (245,218,172), the shirt-cream, is deliberately excluded from 'top' even though it is visually the most obvious second torso color: touchup_m3.py reuses it as the eye highlight (matching m1/F1's 'reuse an existing light color' convention), so remapping it would also recolor the eyes. trousers-main (109,91,44) has a minor, documented seam-boundary leak: ~5-12px per view at the vest/trousers waist transition (rows 23-31) also use this exact tone (belt-shadow blending into the trouser tone) — remapping trousers will very slightly tint those few seam pixels too; visually negligible given their count and boundary position, flagged for Safi's eyes at native atlas scale per the same standard as F1's skirt-hem caveat.

suggestedVariant.name: ochre
suggestedVariant.note: One example remap into the world's muted garment families (BEING_PALETTE_VARIANTS in beingPalette.ts: slate-blue / violet-grey / moss / ochre / bone). M3 ships in a warm brown vest already, so 'ochre' (a related but distinguishable warm family) is proposed for variant testing — re-validate visually against the actual atlas render before locking in for R3.
